results.description: DPG-RR owns a better consensus performance than GT-SAGA and DSGD.
results.evidence:
Run outputs at results/formal/time_invariant_a9a_seed0/metrics.json and results/formal/time_invariant_w8a_seed0/metrics.json contain full per-epoch consensus_D histories for all three methods. Final (epoch 200) values:

a9a: DPG-RR=1.729e-24, GT-SAGA=1.026e+00, DSGD=2.504e-26
w8a: DPG-RR=1.445e-23, GT-SAGA=4.857e-01, DSGD=6.445e-28

DPG-RR > GT-SAGA holds on both datasets (DPG-RR lower consensus_D ✓), but DPG-RR > DSGD fails on both datasets: DSGD has substantially lower consensus_D than DPG-RR on a9a (2.50e-26 < 1.73e-24) and w8a (6.45e-28 < 1.44e-23). The minimum consensus_D values across all epochs confirm the same ordering.
results.note: The claim requires DPG-RR to beat DSGD on consensus_D (lower_is_better). DSGD achieves far lower consensus values than DPG-RR on both datasets in the run outputs, contradicting this part of the claimed ranking.

results.description: Local variables generated by all algorithms (DPG-RR, GT-SAGA, DSGD) achieve consensus (D(x) converges to 0) on a9a and w8a.
results.evidence: Run outputs in results/formal/time_invariant_a9a_seed0/ and results/formal/time_invariant_w8a_seed0/ contain per-epoch consensus_D values for all three algorithms. DPG-RR and DSGD do converge to near-zero consensus: on a9a at epoch 200, dpg_rr=1.73e-24 and dsgd=2.50e-26; on w8a at epoch 200, dpg_rr=1.44e-23 and dsgd=6.45e-28. However, GT-SAGA does NOT achieve consensus: on a9a its final consensus_D values oscillate around 0.75–1.77 (epoch 200 value=1.03), and on w8a they oscillate around 0.49–6.18 (epoch 200 value=0.49). GT-SAGA's consensus_D never approaches 0 on either dataset.
results.note: The claim requires ALL algorithms including GT-SAGA to achieve consensus. GT-SAGA's consensus metric stays O(1) on both datasets throughout 200 epochs, failing the convergence criterion.

results.description: The trajectories of objective function F(x) generated by all algorithms (DPG-RR, GT-SAGA, DSGD) converge quickly to the optimum F* on a9a and w8a.
results.evidence: Results found in results/formal/time_invariant_a9a_seed0/metrics.json and results/formal/time_invariant_w8a_seed0/metrics.json. On a9a: DPG-RR objective oscillates (0.437→0.433→0.442→0.443→0.440→0.443) — no convergence trend; GT-SAGA and DSGD decrease from ~6.8 to ~0.52 but stationarity_norm remains 0.11–0.13 at epoch 200, still far from converged. On w8a: DPG-RR objective *increases* from 0.49 at epoch 1 to 0.64 at epoch 200 (best was 0.45 at epoch 8), indicating divergence; GT-SAGA and DSGD decrease from ~6.1 to ~0.51 but still not plateaued (stationarity_norm ~0.085–0.087 at epoch 200). No F* reference value is stored in any output file. CLAIM_RESULTS.json explicitly labels the claim as 'partially_reproduced' noting 'final objective values and the w8a ranking differ from the paper's plotted behavior.'
results.note: The claim requires all three algorithms to converge 'quickly' to the optimum F* on both datasets. GT-SAGA and DSGD show some decreasing trend but have not reached a stable plateau at 200 epochs, and DPG-RR on w8a is actually diverging after its early minimum. No F* ground-truth is available in outputs, making 'convergence to optimum' impossible to verify directly, but the trajectory shapes themselves do not support the claim of quick convergence.

results.description: DPG-RR converges faster than NEXT and DGM over both a9a and w8a datasets.
results.evidence:
Run outputs from results/formal/time_varying_a9a_seed0/ and results/formal/time_varying_w8a_seed0/ (dpg_rr.csv, next.csv, dgm.csv, metrics.json) confirm DPG-RR converges strictly faster than both NEXT and DGM on both datasets.

a9a (200 epochs): DPG-RR reaches stationarity_norm~0.076 and objective~0.443 (already below 0.5 at epoch 1). NEXT never drops below stationarity 0.1 (final=0.917, objective=1.303). DGM never drops below stationarity 0.1 (final=0.332, objective=0.847).

w8a (200 epochs): DPG-RR reaches stationarity_norm~0.063 and objective~0.641 (first epoch obj<0.5 at epoch 1). NEXT never converges (final stationarity=0.588, objective=4.183). DGM never converges (final stationarity=0.577, objective=3.452).

Both cases (a9a and w8a) satisfy DPG-RR > NEXT and DPG-RR > DGM, fulfilling the 2-of-2 aggregation requirement.
results.note: Convergence speed is assessed via stationarity_norm and objective values at epoch 200, and epoch at which thresholds are first crossed. NEXT and DGM do not approach convergence within 200 epochs on either dataset, while DPG-RR is effectively converged from very early epochs. The CLAIM_RESULTS.json notes "NEXT and DGM were substantially slower on w8a than in the paper's figure" — this corroborates the ranking direction even though absolute numbers differ from the paper.

results.description: DPG-RR shows a better consensus numerical performance than NEXT and DGM on a9a and w8a.
results.evidence:
Run outputs found in results/formal/time_varying_{a9a,w8a}_seed0/{dpg_rr,next,dgm}.csv (metric: consensus_D column).

Final-epoch consensus_D values:
a9a: DPG-RR=1.070e-29, NEXT=8.566e-12, DGM=4.696e-30
w8a: DPG-RR=3.408e-28, NEXT=1.894e-13, DGM=1.345e-29

Minimum consensus_D across all epochs:
a9a: DPG-RR=5.448e-30, NEXT=4.061e-16, DGM=1.430e-30
w8a: DPG-RR=1.452e-28, NEXT=1.894e-13, DGM=6.545e-30

DPG-RR > NEXT (lower_is_better): HOLDS for both a9a and w8a.
DPG-RR > DGM (lower_is_better): FAILS for both a9a and w8a — DGM achieves lower (better) consensus_D than DPG-RR in both datasets.

Aggregation: only 1 of 2 required sub-claims holds (DPG-RR beats NEXT but not DGM), so the overall claim fails.
results.note: The claim requires DPG-RR to beat both NEXT and DGM. DGM consistently achieves a lower consensus error than DPG-RR across all epochs on both datasets, contradicting the claim.

results.description: DPG-RR has a comparable convergence performance of Prox-G on a9a and w8a.
results.evidence: Run outputs from results/formal/time_varying_a9a_seed0/metrics.json and results/formal/time_varying_w8a_seed0/metrics.json confirm both algorithms ran for 200 epochs. On a9a: DPG-RR stationarity norms range 0.029–0.141 throughout training; Prox-G starts at 1.28 but decreases to 0.045 by epoch 200 (comparable at epoch 50: DPG-RR=0.129, Prox-G=0.137). On w8a: DPG-RR converges quickly to ~0.059–0.065 and stays there; Prox-G starts at 0.595 and slowly decreases to 0.075 by epoch 200. Final values are roughly in same order of magnitude (DPG-RR=0.063, Prox-G=0.075). CLAIM_RESULTS.json (C2) also notes "Prox-G was competitive." The a9a case clearly shows comparable convergence. The w8a case shows DPG-RR convergences substantially faster but both reach similar low stationarity norms by epoch 200.
results.note: The "comparable" claim is a qualitative boolean assessment. On a9a the convergence curves are clearly comparable. On w8a DPG-RR converges much faster early on but both end at similar final stationarity norms (~0.063 vs ~0.075), so final convergence performance is broadly comparable. The claim likely refers to final-epoch convergence quality rather than convergence speed throughout training. Confidence is medium because "comparable" is subjective and w8a shows meaningful differences in the convergence trajectory.

results.description: DPG-RR converges faster than DPG-SG on the w8a dataset.
results.evidence: Run outputs in results/formal/sampling_w8a_seed0/metrics.json and dpg_rr.csv/dpg_sg.csv directly contradict the claim. Convergence metrics (stationarity_norm, lower=better/faster): DPG-RR final (epoch 200) = 0.063103; DPG-SG final = 0.053532 — DPG-SG is more converged at the end. Over 200 epochs, DPG-SG has lower stationarity_norm in 105/200 epochs vs DPG-RR in 95/200. Threshold crossings: first epoch below 0.07: RR=8, SG=7; first below 0.06: RR=8, SG=13 (RR transiently better in early epochs only, not sustained); first below 0.055: RR=34, SG=13. The repository's own CLAIM_RESULTS.json (claim C3) explicitly notes: "the experiment…does not reproduce the paper's claimed RR ranking under this independent implementation." No explicit convergence_speed scalar is stored in the outputs, but all available proxies (stationarity_norm trajectory, epoch-wise win counts, final values) show DPG-SG converging at least as fast or faster than DPG-RR on w8a.
results.note: The metrics.json contains no explicit "convergence_speed" field; verdict is based on stationarity_norm trajectories which are the standard proxy for convergence in these experiments. The CLAIM_RESULTS.json authored by the reproduction itself confirms the ranking claim is not supported.

results.description: DPG-IG shows a comparable convergence rate with DPG-RR on the w8a dataset.
results.evidence: results/formal/sampling_w8a_seed0/metrics.json (experiment="sampling", dataset="w8a"): Over 200 epochs, DPG-IG and DPG-RR show closely matched convergence. Stationarity norms at key epochs — epoch 10: RR=0.070445, IG=0.076891 (ratio 1.09); epoch 50: RR=0.059252, IG=0.065146 (ratio 1.10); epoch 100: RR=0.065089, IG=0.063658 (ratio 0.978); epoch 200: RR=0.063103, IG=0.061696 (ratio 0.978). Objective values at epoch 200: RR=0.641168, IG=0.659121 (ratio 1.028). Both methods converge at nearly the same rate throughout training, with IG never more than ~10% worse than RR in stationarity norm at any measured epoch.
results.note: The comparison is based on stationarity_norm and objective values from the sampling_w8a_seed0 run, which matches experiment id exp3_ablation_sampling. DPG-SG is also present in the outputs but is not relevant to this claim.
